label: Critiqued Quijano's "coloniality of power" for assuming biological gender naturalism
description: In "Heterosexualism and the Colonial/Modern Gender System" (2007), María Lugones exposed Quijano's model of coloniality as blind to the colonial invention of binary sex/gender itself, formulating the "coloniality of gender."
dialecticalTension: Corrects decolonial theory's gender blindness by centering Indigenous and Black feminist archives.

citations.author: María Lugones
citations.work: Heterosexualism and the Colonial/Modern Gender System

label: Transformed Anzaldúa's borderlands into "world-travelling" and coalitional praxis
description: Drawing directly on Gloria Anzaldúa's mestiza consciousness, Lugones conceptualized "curdling" (versus purity logic) and playful "world-travelling" as epistemological tools for women-of-color solidarity.
dialecticalTension: Turns borderland hybridity into a method of anti-fragmentation political coalition.

citations.author: María Lugones
citations.work: Pilgrimages / Peregrinajes: Theorizing Coalition Against Multiple Oppressions

label: Formulated the "coloniality of gender" framework of modern-colonial domination
description: Lugones coined the coloniality of gender to show how European colonialism imposed dimorphic biological sex, racialized dehumanization, and compulsory heterosexuality onto colonized societies.
dialecticalTension: Integrates decolonial world-systems critique with radical feminist ontology.

label: Converged on non-essentialist Latin American decolonial feminist critique
description: Lugones and Rivera Cusicanqui form twin pillars of Latin American decolonial feminism—combining Lugones's "curdling" against purity with Rivera Cusicanqui's ch'ixi coexistence of unassimilated worlds.
dialecticalTension: Debates academic decoloniality while defending resistant Indigenous-feminist multiplicity.
